**Applicability (all 50 items scored, nothing N/A).** Human subjects met on E1 (`description`: ICU/PICU/NICU admissions; keywords “critical care”, “clinical notes”) and E8 — opening Element 4 sub-elements 1–5. The governance condition (E2 `confidentiality_level: restricted`, controlled access under signed agreement) independently met, and would alone have opened 4.1–4.2. Datasets-shared met on E2 (`distribution_formats` + `third_party_sharing.is_shared: true`); access-by-approval resolved to applicable under the ambiguity rule. Software-output met on `external_resources` → github.com/chorus-ai, opening 8.3; 8.4 scored under #1081 as processing is established.

**Drivers of the score.** Funding (5/5: `OT2OD032701` validates against the NIH activity-code/institute/serial pattern, RePORTER ID consistent across three fields) and technical transparency (5/5) are the strengths; 8.4 was earned on *processing-role* software — OHNLP tokenisation, `chorus_waveform` conversion, DeGauss/UF-Geocoding — not on `chorus-extract-upload` (capture) or `CHoRUSReports` (validation), which I explicitly declined to rely on. Losses cluster in three places: human-subjects governance documented as programme activity rather than oversight (no IRB, no consent or waiver, no DPIA, despite `involves_human_subjects: true` and PICU/NICU patients) → 4.1 and 4.4 = 0; complete absence of version tracking for a self-described “partially released”, growing dataset → E6 1/5; and no persistent ID, DOI, citation or publisher → 1.1, 10.1, 10.2 = 0. Four consistency checks failed, 12 passed, 6 warnings.

The record's candour is noted as a strength in its own right (it adjudicates a tier-2/tier-4 count conflict openly, flags the overloaded `OTHER` enum, reproduces source typos) — but candour about an absent IRB does not convert the absence into documentation, so it did not earn the points.
